PREAMBLE, SHORT TITLE,  
COMMENCEMENT AND APPLICATION

Vidyashilp  University  is  the  culmination  of  an  outstanding  legacy  of  the  Vidyashilp   
Education  Group,  committed  to  excellence  in  education.  Vidyashilp  University  aims  to   
foster an environment and culture of collaboration, responsiveness, high performance an d  
service. We are people -centred and  have a  strongly desire to provide a unique Vidyashilp  
Experience to our students and staff, focused on nurturing students who will become self - 
aware, confident, empathetic and resourceful leaders who will serve society to the best of  
their abilities.

The VU Experience fosters a climate for collaboration between individuals and groups from  
diverse  cultures  and  backgrounds.  VU  creates  a  diverse,  inclusive  community  and   
environment where VU faculty, staff, students and parents, and alumni feel connected t o  
one another by a common sense of purpose, pride, and spirit, and develop a distinctive  
ability to work, learn, lead and serve in diverse contexts.

VU’s primary educational goal is the cultivation of deep domain knowledge within each  
student’s chosen field. We believe that investing in all domains of our differentiated focus  
areas is essential to create intellectual capital to drive progress and achieve excellence.  At  
VU, our schools don’t function in silos but rather with an interdisciplinary dependence.  
We  focus  on  a  problem -solving  approach  and  provide  program  choices  across  all  four   
schools with a curriculum established in Data Science, Digital Business, Design Studies,  
Legal Studies and Liberal Arts.
VISION, MISSION AND  CORE VALUES

OUR VISION   
We   aspire   to   provide   meaningful,   collective   learning   experiences   that   result   in    
conscientious leadership for a progressive, yet sustainable society.   
OUR MISSION   
x  We inspire people locally, nationally and  globally  by extending access to Vidyashilp  
University’s  innovative  teaching  and  resources  through  inclusive  and  flexible   
opportunities to study and research.   
x  To  develop  human  values  and  human  potential  to  its  fullest  extent  so  that   
intellectually  capable  and  imaginatively  gifted  leaders  can  emerge  in  a  range  of   
professions.  
1

OUR VALUES   
INTEGRITY   –  We  embrace  integrity  as  a  central  value  in  all  aspects  of  personal  and   
professional engagement  – including learning, teaching, governance and service  – to instil  
a culture of trust and accountability.

ACADEMIC FREEDOM  – We affirm the principles of academic freedom for both students  
and teachers, their  rights and responsibilities to advance knowledge through research and  
creativity, and to educate students to develop their own independence of mind.

DIVERSITY,  EQUITY  AND  INCLUSION   –  We  assert  that  diversity  and  interplay  of   
differences is essential to educational excellence and to enrich the individual and collective  
learning experiences.   
Short Title, Commencement and Application

a.  These Regulations shall be called Academic Regulations .  
b.  They shall come into force with immediate effect.    
c.  The  Academic  Regulations  are  applicable  to  all  existing  Degree  and  Diploma   
Programs of the University. Any amendments made therein, shall also be applicable  
to new Degree and Diploma Programs that may be offered by the University in the  
future .

d.  Specific  aspects  of  the  Regulations  pertaining  to  a  particular  Degree  Program  are   
given separately along with the concerned Program Regulations.

e.  These  Regulations  may  evolve  and  get  amended  or  modified  or  changed  through   
appropriate approvals from the Academic Council, from time to time, and shall be  
binding on all concerned.

f.  Additional Regulations, if any, prescribed by the Regulatory / Statutory Bodies for  
a   particular   Degree   Program   shall   be   included   in   the   concerned   Program    
Regulations.       
Definitions
u)  “Section” means duly numbered Sections of these Regulations;
v)  “Statutes” means the Statues of Vidyashilp University;
w)  “Sub -Clause” means duly numbered Sub -Clauses of these Regulations;

x)  "Summer Term” means an additional academic term conducted during the summer  
break (typically in June -July) for a duration of about eight (08) calendar weeks;

y)  “University / VU” means Vidyashilp University; and   
z)  “Vice Chancellor” means the Vice Chancellor of the Uni versity.

ADMISSION RULES, FEE POLICY, AND  
SCHOLARSHIP POLICY

1 
ADMISSION 
Admission to the University shall be open to all persons irrespective of caste, class, 
creed, gender, abilities, or nationality. All admissions shall be made on the basis 
of  merit  in  the  qualifying  examinations  and  as  per  the rules  and guidelines 
prescribed  by  the  Government  of  Karnataka,  other  concerned regulatory  bodies 
and the entrance examinations conducted by the University. 
The  students  shall  be  admitted  to  a  Program  subject  to  fulfilment  of  eligibility 
criteria, as prescribed by the University for the respective Program. 
A student admitted to a Program of study, shall continue to remain registered for 
such a Program, till they successfully complete the Program or withdraw from the 
Program in accordance with the concerned Program Regulations. 
Every student duly admitted to the University for a Program after compliance with 
prescribed  formalities  and  payment  of  prescribed  fees  as  applicable  and  other 
amounts and submission of prescribed documents and certificates shall be allotted 
a University Enrolment Number OR UEN. 
If a student fails to pay the University Fee, or fails to produce all the mandatory 
documents  and  certificates  required  for  admission  to  the  University  before  the 
prescribed last date, the Provisional Offer of Admission to the student shall stand 
withdrawn. 
If a student desires to join the University on the basis of Lateral Entry or Transfer 
of  Credits  from  other  Institutes/Universities  during  the  Program, they shall  be 
examined for eligibility for admission as per the procedure and criteria laid down 
in  the  Academic  Regulations  of  the  University  and  the  concerned  Program 
Regulations, and admission shall be dependent on their eligibility so determined. 
Confirmation of admission and enrolment in the University is subject to fulfilment 
of the eligibility criteria. 
2 FEE POLICY 
a. The  University  fee  consists  of  components  such  as  Tuition  Fee,  Security  Deposit 
(Refundable), Examination Fee, Convocation Fee and such other components as may 
be prescribed by the Board of Management from time to time. 
b. Every  program  of  the  University  has  a  prescribed  University  Fee.  Further  the  Fee 
Structure and the payment schedule for the entire duration of the concerned program 
is announced by way of notification before the commencement of each academic year. 
c. The  Tuition  Fee  always  means  the  Annual  Tuition  Fee  for an academic  year  for  a 
program. The Annual Tuition Fee does not include the expenses / charges for extra- 
curricular  activities,  local  /  international  educational  trips  and  other  value-added 
programs that may be introduced from time to time. 
7

d.  The S ecurity Deposit is a Refundable Security Deposit without any interest, subject  
to deduction of outstanding dues if any, after the student graduates from the program  
or discontinues from the program or for whatever the reason(s) .  
e.  The Payment Schedule of the University Fee must be strictly adhered to, by all the  
students.  Failure  to  comply  shall  result  in  the  student  not  being  eligible  for   
registration to the concerned academic year  and late fee will be charged accordingly .  
Further, the students are cautioned that this could lead to the loss of an academic  
year.  
f.  Vidyashilp University shall not be obliged to send any reminders for payment of the  
University  Fee.  If  it  is  done,  it  is  only  in  the  interest  of  students  and  cannot  be   
demanded or referred to in the event of failure to pay the University Fee as per the  
spe cified schedule.   
g.  The  University  Fee  Structure  is  subject  to  change  from  time  to  time  and  shall  be   
notified by the University. The University’s decision regarding changes in fee structure  
is final and binding on all concerned.
a.  For Students who seek admission directly in the University:

Students who seek admission directly for a specific program  in  the University shall be  
notified  of the prescribed University Fee and schedule of payment for first year and  
subsequent years in the Provisional Admission Letter. Failure to remit the fee as per  
the specified payment schedule or commencement of each academic year, shall result  
in the forfei ture of admission to the program  and applicability of late fee accordingly  
as decided by the University time to time .

b.  For General Students admitted through CET of Government of Karnataka:   
[i]   The  Fee  Structure  (Engineering  Fee  Structure  for  CET  Fee)  for  students   
admitted  through  CET  shall  be  as  notified  by  the  Karnataka  Examinations   
Authority (KEA).  First year’s tuition fee shall be remitted to the CET -KEA at  
the time of counselling / seat se lection.   
[ii]               On  reporting to the University for confirmation of admission to the concerned  
program, the student shall also remit “other fee s” as notified by the University   
from time to time .   
[iii]        Subsequent  years’  tuition   and   other  fee s  shall  be  remitted  directly  to  the   
University  on  or  before  the  notified  last  date.  Failure  to  remit  “other  fee s”  
notified  by  the  university,  shall  result  in  the  forfeiture  of  admission  to  the   
program  and charge of the late fee as may be prescribed .  
c.  For category (SC/ST/others as specified by KEA) students admitted through CET of  
Government of Karnataka:   
8

[i]          The Fee Structure (Engineering Fee Structure for CET Fee) for students admitted  
through  CET  shall  be  as  notified  by  the  Karnataka  Examinations  Authority   
(KEA).     
[ii]      On reporting to the University for confirmation of admission to the concerned  
program, the student shall remit “other fee s” as notified by the University.  
[iii]      Further,  such  student(s)  shall  compulsorily  require  to  apply  for/renew  the   
Scholarship  as  notified  by  the  Government  of  Karnataka.    Upon  receipt  of   
scholarship from the Government of Karnataka, such Student(s) shall promptly  
remit the scholarship amount to wards the fee to the University within five (05)  
working days  on receipt of the scholarship from the Government of Karnataka .    
It is the sole responsibility of the student(s) to comply with the norms for payment of Fee  
within the stipulated time. Failure to pay the University Fee / scholarship amount as per  
the  specified  schedule  shall  result  in  (i)  the  student  being  declared  inel igible  for   
registration to the term end exams, which could result in loss of an academic year ; (ii) levy  
late fee  for late remittance(s) ; (iii) in case of SC/ST/OBC students, a Report will be sent to  
the  Government  of  Karnataka  about  non -remittance  of  scholarship  amount  to  the   
University towards the fee  and  misuse of the same.

a.  All fee payments should necessarily be made online  only  using the login credentials  
of the fee portal as instructed by the University from time to time.   
b.  The Fee is payable in INR only   
c.  The University will not accept Cash, DD and Cheque.   
d.  The digital receipt will be generated by the online system subject to realization of  
payments.  
e.  All  statutory  taxes  /  government  levies,  convenience  charges  and  bank  charges   
pertaining to inward remittance of any fee, if any , shall be borne by the  payer.   
f.  The University shall not be responsible for any fee amount returned to the  payer  
(Student)   without  being  credited  to  Vidyashilp  University  bank  account.  In  such   
cases, late fee  as may be prescribed  shall be applicable till  the  date of receipt of  the  
fee by Vidyashilp University.   
g.  It  shall  be  the  sole  responsibility  of  the  student  to  ensure  that  the  fee  payment   
process is completed  with in  the  specified time.   
In case a student is required to repeat/re -register  for  an Academic Year, the Annual Fee  
payable by her/him shall correspond to the Academic Year to be repeated, and shall be  
as per the Fee Policy in force at that point of time.   
The  policies  relating  to  the  University  Fee  and  Deposits,  where  applicable,  are  the   
prerogative  of  Vidyashilp  University  and  may  be  revised  by  the  University  from  time  to   
time. Such changes shall be binding on all  concerned.

5   FEE CONCESSION AND SCHOLARSHIP POLICY  
Introduction:  
Vidyashilp  University  is  committed   for   providing  the  best  education  opportunities  to   
motivated students. The University has established various categories of scholarships to  
encourage and enable students to pursue education at Vidyashilp University.    
Scholarships are provided to reward and support meritorious and talented students, who  
have  demonstrated  exceptional  performance  in  academics,  sports   and  co-curricular  
activities. The University is particularly committed to enabling meritorious students with  
financial  constraints,  differently  abled  students  and  achievers  at  the  state  and  national   
levels, through appropriate scholarships.    
5.1  Categories of Scholarships

To cater to the different needs and circumstances of meritorious students, the University  
offers f our  (0 4)  categories  of Scholarships.
5.1.1  Merit -based Scholarship at  the time of  Admission

Merit   scholarships   are   awarded   to   students   with   outstanding   academic    
performance. This scholarship is awarded at the time of admission to the 1 
st 
 year  
of a program.
Two (02) sub -categories of Merit Scholarships are offered:

5.1.2  Outstanding  achievement  in  State  /  National  /  International  Level  Entrance   
Examinations:

This Scholarship is awarded based on the performance in the State / National /  
International Level Entrance Examinations specified for a particular program.
5.1.3  Meritorious Performance in the Qualifying Examination:

The   Scholarship   is   awarded   based   on   the   performance   in   the   Qualifying    
Examinations (State / National / International Boards).  The details of the extent  
of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are as per the scholarship  
policy  and subject to approval by the Scholarship Committee .

The University is committed to ensure that a meritorious student is not hindered  
from pursuing education at Vidyashilp due to financial constraints.
Three (03) sub -categories of enabling scholarships are offered:
5.2.1  Low Income Based Scholarship

This scholarship is offered to enable meritorious students whose family income is  
a constraint to meet the tuition fees of the program.
5.2.2  Single Parent  (Mother)  Income Based Scholarship .

This  Scholarship  is  specifically  offered  to  a  student  with  Single   Parent  (Mother)   
having financial constraints to pursue education at Vidyashilp.
5.2.3  Ex -Service Parent Income Based Scholarship

This scholarship is offered to a meritorious student whose parent (father/mother)  
is  an  ex-service personnel with financial constraints.

The definition of ex -service is specific to commissioned/non -commissioned staff of  
the Armed Forces and staff of the Central/State Police Services.

5.2.4  The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are  
as  per  the  scholarship  policy  and  subject  to  approval  by  the  Scholarship   
Committee.
5.3      Encouragement Scholarship

This scholarship is awarded to recognize and encourage  students  who have excelled in  
various sports / culture /  fine arts/ s ciences and have participated / been awarded at  
State/ National / International levels.

The  University  is  also  committed  to  encourage  differently -abled  students   to  pursue   
education at Vidyashilp University.
Two (02) sub -categories of Encouragement Scholarships are offered:

5.3.1  Scholarship  for  Outstanding  performance  in  the  fields  of   Sports/Culture/Fine  
Arts/Sciences.
5.3.2  Scholarship for Differently -Abled.

5.3.3   The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are  
as  per  the  scholarship  policy   and  subject  to  approval  by  the  Scholarship   
Committee.

5.4  Academic Performance Scholarship (During the Program)   
To  reward  and  motivate  excellence  in  overall  academic  performance,  scholarships  are   
awarded  to  the  selected  outstanding  students  during  the  program  i.e.,  from  2nd  Year   
onwards. The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility crit eria  
are as per the scholarship policy and subject to approval by the Scholarship Committee.
5.5  General Terms and Conditions

a)  All  types  of  Scholarships  shall  be  applicable  only  on  the  Tuition  Fee  for  the   
concerned academic year.   
b)  A student shall be eligible for only one scholarship in a given academic year.   
c)  All types of Scholarships shall be valid only for the concerned academic year.    
d)  Renewal of any type  of   scholarship is not automatic and shall be governed by the  
terms and criteria as mentioned in this policy.   
e)  The number of Scholarships to be awarded under each type and sub -category for  
the concerned academic year shall be solely decided by the Board of Management  
on the recommendation of the University Scholarship Committee.   
f)  A  student  who  has  been  selected  for  a  scholarship  shall  provide  a  joint  (with   
parent) undertaking .

The scholarship shall be terminated and the scholarship amount shall be returned to the  
University, in case of the following violations;
Further, such a student shall not be eligible to re -apply for any University scholarship.

a)  During Admissions:   
i)  Eligible  candidates  may  submit  the  scholarship  application  form  with  all   
relevant documents to the admission office.     
ii)  The  University Scholarship  Committee shall scrutinize and shortlist candidates  
to be interviewed by the Committee.   
iii)  The award of scholarship shall be recommended by the University Scholarship  
Committee for the approval of the Vice Chancellor.   
iv)  The decision of the Vice Chancellor shall be final.   
b)  During the Program:   
i)  The   University   Scholarship   Committee   shall   invite   applications   at   the    
commencement   of   an   academic   year   for   the   Academic   Performance    
Scholarships  which  are  awarded  based  on  performance  during  the  previous   
academic year.    
ii)  The   committee   shall   also   invite   applications   for   renewal   of   Enabling,    
Encouraging  Scholarships  which was provided at the time of admissions and  
the same shall be subject to review by the Scholarship Committee .  
The committee shall recommend the list of scholarship awardees to the Vice Chancellor  
for approval  and the decision of the Vice -Chancellor shall be final .

1.1.  The academic activities of the University are regulated by the Academic  
Calendar  approved  by  the  Academic  Council  and  notified  by  the   
University at least one calendar month before the commencement of each  
academic year.

1.2.  An  academic  year  in  the  University  shall  normally  be  divided  into  two   
semesters consisting of ninety (90) University working days each, known  
as ‘Odd Semester’ (normally from July / August to December) and ‘Even  
Semester’ (normally from January to April/May).  
1.3.  An  additional  Academic  Term  known  as  the  ‘Summer  Term’  may  be   
scheduled during the  summer break (June to July).   
2.  Registration

2.1.  Every student shall complete the mandatory requirement known as the  
‘Registration’  procedure  and  register  for  the  prescribed  and  approved   
Courses to be pursued during a given Academic Term. This Registration  
process   is   mandatory   every   Semester   /   Academic   Term   till   the    
completion of the Program.  The University Registrar's Office manages the  
registration process and related activities.

2.2.  The prescribed date for Registration shall be announced in the Academic  
Calendar  and  through  notifications  issued  by  the  University  to  this   
effect.

2.3.  The  Chairperson  of   the  Program  Academic  Committee  (PAC)  of  each   
Program/School  shall  communicate  the  list  of  approved/prescribed   
Courses  available  for  Registration  in  the  concerned  Semester  to  the   
University Registrar's Office for Notification as per the specified dates in  
the Academic Calendar.

2.4.  Every student after consulting  their  Faculty Advisor [Mentor]  is required  
to register for the approved Courses offered  in the given Academic Term  
at  the  commencement  of  each  Semester/Academic  Term  on  the  days   
fixed  for  such  registration  as  notified  in  the  Academic  Calendar  or  the   
University Notification to this effect.

On  joining  the  University,  each  student  is  assigned  a   Faculty  Advisor   
[Mentor]   to  counsel  the  student  on  matters  related  to  the  Registration   
process.

Without  registration,  any  academic  activity  (Course  /  Internship  / 
Project,  etc.)  undergone  by  a  student  will  not  be  counted  towards  the 
requirements for the award of the Degree. No student shall be permitted 
to  attend  classes  without  completing  the  appropriate  registration 
procedure. 
15

2.6.  Late  registration  shall  only  be  permitted  in  case  of   medical  exigencies,   
specifically  hospitalization,  trauma  or  contagious  disease s,  for  the   
student    /    family    member ,    and    participation    in    approved     
competitions/events as detailed in Sub -Clauses 2.6.1 and 2.6.2. below .  
In such cases, a student may be permitted for late registration with prior  
approval  from  the  concerned  Program  Chair  /  Dean  of  the  concerned   
School.   In the absence of Program Chair / Dean of the concerned School,  
the authorised faculty shall approve.

2.6.1.  In  cases  of  medical  exigency  (viz.  hospitalization,  trauma  or   
contagious  disease  only),   for  the  student  /  family  member,   the   
maximum period permissible for late registration shall  not  be more  
than  two  (02)  calendar  weeks  counted  from  the  specified  date  of   
Registration  announced  by  the  University.    The  student  must   
produce  the  medical  certificates,  medical  prescriptions,  hospital   
discharge  report,  medical  fitness  report  and  all  such  rele vant  
documents  duly  attested  by  the  concerned  registered  medical   
officer  of  the  hospital  where  the  concerned  student  /  family   
member was hospitalized or medically treated. The student shall  
not be eligible for late registration if  they fail to produce authentic  
medical  certificates  and  relevant  documents  in  support  of  the   
medical exigency.   
2.6.2.  If a student of second and subsequent semesters has been  selected  
/ permitted  by the University to participate in State / National /  
International Competitions / Events, the concerned student may  
be permitted for late registration.  The student must produce duly  
attested  documents  and/or  Certificates  to  be  eligible  for  the   
provisio n  of  late  registration.  The  number  of  days  for  which  the   
concerned student shall be given permission for late registration  
shall  be  approved  by  the  Vice  Chancellor  on  recommendation  of   
both  the  Director,  Campus  Life  and  Program  Chair  of  the   
concerned school.   
2.7.  In  case  of  any  other  reason  for  late  registration  other  than  the  cases   
specified   in   Sub -Clauses   2.6.1   and   2.6.2   above,   the   maximum    
permissible period for late registration shall not be more than one (01)  
calendar week counted from the specified date of Registration announced  
by the University.

Further, the student shall pay a Late Fee for late registration as specified  
by  the  University  at  the  commencement  of  the  Academic  Term.  No   
16

relaxation whatsoever shall be given on attendance requirement in case  
of  late  registration.  Under  no  circumstances  shall  such  a  student  be   
permitted to register for the Academic Term after the permissible period  
for late registration of one (01) calendar week counted from the specified  
date of Registration.

2.8.  Further, the provisions mentioned in Clauses 2.6 and 2.7 are applicable  
only for registration at the commencement of a Semester and does not  
apply for the Summer Term (Refer Section 11).   
2.9.  Students  are  not  permitted  to  re -register  for  Courses  which  they  have   
already passed, except under the provisions and conditions of Clauses  
11.4.3 and 12.5.

2.10.  A student shall be permitted to register in the next Semester only if all  
the following conditions are fulfilled:

2.10.1.  The student has paid all specified fees of the University as per the  
University Fee Policy and payment schedule.   
2.10.2.  The  student  has  cleared  all  University,  Hostel,  Transport  and   
Library dues (if any).   
2.10.3.  The  student  has  not  been  debarred  from  registering  on  any   
specific grounds by the University.    
2.11.  Further,  the  student  must  fulfil  the  progression  criteria  prescribed  in   
Clause  12.1  to  register   for  the  Semester  at  the  commencement  of  the   
concerned Academic Year.

2.12.  A  student  who  is  eligible  for  registration,  but  fails  to  register  for  the   
Academic Term within the specified dates,  including the late registration  
date,  shall be removed from the rolls for the concerned Academic Term  
and shall not be permitted to attend classes for the concerned Academic  
Term.  Such  a  student  shall  have  to  register  for  the  corresponding   
Academic Term in the next academic year.

2.13.  Pre-Registration  (Specialization  /  Minor  /  Open  and  other  specified   
Courses) for higher Semesters:

All students (other than the students admitted to the first Semester of a  
Program) intending to register for the next higher Semester are required  
to  complete  the  Pre -Registration  process.  A  student,  after  consultation   
with the  Faculty Advisor  [Mentor], is required to declare  their  intent to  
17

register  for  Specialization  /  Minor  /  Open  and  any  other  specified   
Courses, as/if applicable, well in advance, before the actual start of the  
concerned  Academic  Term,  through  the  process  of  Pre -Registration  as   
per the schedule/dates announced in the Academic Calendar and/or the  
notifications  issued  by  the  University  to  this  effect.  Specialization  /   
Minor  courses  will  be  offered  only  if   a  minimum  of  ten  (10)  students   
register for the same. However, the program chair may permit to offer the  
courses at their discretion.

For a student to register for some Courses, it may be required either to  
have  exposure  in,  or  to  have  completed  satisfactorily,  or  to  have  prior   
earned  credits  in  some  specified  Courses.  Such  Course  pre -requisites  
shall be specified in the concerned Program  Regulations / Course Plan  
as approved by the PAC.
2.15.  Changes in Registration: Add/Drop

Students  may  add  and  drop  Courses  after  consulting  the  concerned   
Faculty  Advisors  [Mentor]   and  submit  a  request  for  add/drop  to  the

3.  Academic Credits - Course Credit Structure    
The Credit Structure is used to define various types of Courses to provide for  
the  appropriate  pedagogy  and  methods  of  assessment  and  evaluation.  The   
flexibility required to accomplish the Course learning objectives and outcomes  
can be provided for, while retaining a common framework for Credit allocation.  
More  importantly,  it  is  necessary  to  have  a  transparent,  credible  and  robust   
system  for  planning,  delivery  and  evaluation  of  each  Course  of  the  diverse   
Programs of study of the University.   
3.1.  The Credit Structure for defining and categorizing Courses is the L – T –  
P (Lecture  – Tutorial –  Practical) framework. The Course Credits are fixed  
based on the following norms:   
Lecture  /  Tutorial:  One  (01)  contact/classroom  hour  per  week  is   
assigned One (01) Credit.   
Practical:  Two  (02)  hours  per  week  of  practice/studio/laboratory/field   
and other similar practice or skill development components, are assigned  
One (01) Credit.    
For example:   
A Course with L – T – P structure of 4 – 0 – 0 will be assigned 4 Credits.   
A Course with L – T – P structure of 3 – 1 – 0 will be assigned 4 Credits.   
A Course with L – T – P structure of 0 – 0 – 4 will be assigned 2 Credits.   
A Course with L – T – P structure of 1 – 0 – 4 will be assigned 3 Credits.   
3.2.  Practice/Skill   based   Courses   like   Industry   Internship,   Capstone,    
Research  Dissertation,  Integrative  Studio,  Interdisciplinary  Project  and   
such  similar  Courses,  and    Non -Taught  Credit  Courses  like  Seminar,   
Summer  /  Short  Internship,  Social  Engagement  /  Field  Projects  and   
such similar Courses, where the pedagogy does not lend itself to a typical  
L-T-P  structure  as  defined  in  Clause  3.1,  are  assigned  the  number  of   
Credits  based  on  the  quantum  of  work/effort  required  to  fulfil  the   
learning objectives and outcomes prescribed for the concerned Courses.

3.3.  A student earns credits by satisfactorily completing Courses and other  
academic activities every Academic Term. The credits associated with a  
Course are dependent upon the number of hours of instruction per week  
in  that  Course.  Similarly,  the  credit  associated  with  any  of  the  other   
learning activities is dependent upon the quantum of work expected to  
be put in for each of the other learning activities. In general, a certain  
quantum of academic work measured in terms of Credits is laid down as  
the minimum requirements for the award of a particular Degree.

1.  Introduction   
The  Sexual  Harassment  of  Women  at  Workplace  (Prevention,  Prohibition  and  Redressal)   
Act, 2013 ("POSH Act") was enacted as a comprehensive legislation to provide a safe, secure  
and enabling environment, free from sexual harassment to every woman. This statu te was  
enacted to fill the legislative void which had been partially addressed by the judiciary in  
Vishaka and Others v. State of Rajasthan and Others (1997 (7) SCC 323). In this seminal  
public interest litigation verdict, the Supreme Court of India had fr amed a set of guidelines  
("Vishaka Guidelines") for dealing with instances of sexual harassment at the workplace,  
which has now been codified in the POSH Act.   
The Supreme Court of India held that sexual harassment of women is a violation of the  
fundamental right of women to work in a safe environment.    
The Supreme Court has defined ‘sexual harassment’ to include:   
1.1  "An unwanted conduct with sexual undertones if it occurs or which is persistent and  
which demeans, humiliates or creates a hostile and intimidating environment or is  
calculated to induce submission by actual or threatened adverse consequences and  
includes  any one or more or all of the following unwelcome acts or behavior (whether  
directly or by implication), namely;  -   
a)  any unwelcome physical, verbal or non - verbal conduct of sexual nature;   
b)  demand or request for sexual favours;   
c)  making sexually colored remarks   
d)  physical contact and advances; or   
e)  showing pornography

a)  implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment as quid pro quo for sexual

It also serves as a formal reference for determining eligibility to receive the degree 
certificate during convocation. The transcript provides detailed information on

10.1.  The University is committed to keep the entire process of evaluation   
transparent. Within three (03) working days of announcement of results,  
if a student needs clarification on the marks / grade obtained, the Course  
instructor shall explain to a student why they received the grade awarded.

system.

Appeal  Board]  before  the  date  specified  in  the  Academic  Calendar  or   
notification issued by the University to this effect.

Code of Conduct   
1.  Introduction    
The Vidyashilp University Student Code of Conduct is a set of standards of conduct  
expected of students during their tenure as students of the University.     
The  aim  of  the  University  is  to  sculpt  ‘ vidya ’  (education)  and  not  the  student.  In   
Sanskrit,  it  is  said  that  ‘ vidya  dadati  vinayam ’,  meaning,  that  education  imparts   
character. The aim, therefore, is reflective of the need for students to learn values such  
as  respect  for  fellow  beings  as  well  as  display  civility  and  inclusiveness  in  their   
behavior towards other students, faculty, research scholars and support staff.    
At  VU,  the  various  Schools  function  with  an  interdisciplinary  interdependence.   
Diversity in thinking and using a pluralistic approach to learning is something that is  
replete in the University system. A VU graduate must inculcate a sense of reverence  
for t he knowledge derived from other domains.    
The  VU  curriculum  is  structured  such  that,  along  with  domain  knowledge  the   
students  must  learn  aspects  of  citizenship,  sportsmanship  and  concern  for  the   
environment.    
2.  Unique “VU Experience ”  
The  essence  of  Vidyashilp  University  is  to  create  a  unique  “VU  Experience”   –  an  
enjoyable  journey  of  learning  from  one  another  and  learning  together  through   
intentional  collaboration  between  individuals  and  groups  from  diverse  cultures  and   
backgrounds.    
VU’s  purpose  is  to  create  a  diverse,  inclusive  community  and  environment  where   
faculty, staff, students and parents, and alumni feel connected to one another by a  
common sense of purpose and develop a distinctive ability to lead and serve in diverse  
contexts.   
The “VU Experience” is a collective endeavour to inculcate the  “Vidyashilp Graduate  
Attributes” .

it  applies  to   conduct  when  students  participate  in  the  University’s  programs  or

Pursuant  to  the  directives  of  the  Honourable  Supreme  Court  of  India  and  in   
accordance with the UGC Regulations, on curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher  
Educational Institutions, 2009, the University is committed to ensuring no ragging  
takes place by instituting stringent anti -ragging measures and provisions for strict  
punishments to defaulters. Ragging is a cognizable offence and Vidyashilp University  
will take strict action against offenders.   
2.  Definition of Ragging    
The University considers the definition of ragging as per UGC’s “Curbing the menace  
of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions (third amendment), Regulations, 2016”  
which states that:   
" Any act of physical or mental abuse (including bullying and exclusion) targeted at  
another student (fresher or otherwise) on the ground of color, race, religion, caste,  
ethnicity,    gender    (including    transgender),    sexual    orientation,    appearance,     
nationalit y, regional origins, linguistic identity, place of birth, place of residence or  
economic background.”

of each academic year about the Anti -Ragging Policy and zero tolerance for ragging  
at the University.

Guidelines on Prevention of Sexual Harassment 
1. Introduction 
The Sexual  Harassment  of  Women  at  Workplace (Prevention,  Prohibition  and  Redressal) 
Act, 2013 ("POSH Act") was enacted as a comprehensive legislation to provide a safe, secure 
and enabling environment, free from sexual harassment to every woman. This statute was 
enacted to fill the legislative void which had been partially addressed by the judiciary in 
Vishaka and Others v. State of Rajasthan and Others (1997 (7) SCC 323). In this seminal 
public interest litigation verdict, the Supreme Court of India had framed a set of guidelines 
("Vishaka Guidelines") for dealing with instances of sexual harassment at the workplace, 
which has now been codified in the POSH Act. 
The Supreme Court of India held that sexual harassment of women is a violation of the 
fundamental right of women to work in a safe environment. 
The Supreme Court has defined ‘sexual harassment’ to include: 
1.1 "An unwanted conduct with sexual undertones if it occurs or which is persistent and 
which demeans, humiliates or creates a hostile and intimidating environment or is 
calculated to induce submission by actual or threatened adverse consequences and 
includes any one or more or all of the following unwelcome acts or behavior (whether 
directly or by implication), namely; - 
a)  any unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature; 
b)  demand or request for sexual favours; 
c)   making sexually colored remarks 
d)  physical contact and advances; or 
e)   showing pornography 
1.2 any one  (or  more  than  one  or   all) of  the  following circumstances,  if  it occurs or  is 
present in relation or connected with any behavior that has explicit or implicit sexual 
undertones- 
a)  implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment as quid pro quo for sexual 
favors; 
b)  implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in the conduct of work; 
c)   implied  or  explicit  threat  about  the  present  or  future  status  of  the  person 
concerned; 
d)  creating an intimidating offensive or hostile learning environment; 
57

e)  humiliating  treatment  likely  to  affect  the  health,  safety  dignity  or  physical   
integrity of the person concerned;   
As a follow -up to the POSH Act, the University Grants Commission (UGC)  – the apex  
body  for  all  higher  education  institutions   -  has  come  up  with  a  regulation  titled   
University  Grants  Commission  (Prevention,  prohibition  and  redressal  of  sexual   
harassment  of   women  employees  and  students  in  higher  educational  institutions)   
Regulations,  2015.  These  regulations  apply  to  all  higher  education  institutions  in   
India. The provisions of the regulation are being adhered to by Vidyashilp University.     
2.  Responsibility of the University   
VU  commits  to  a  zero -tolerance  policy  against  sexual  harassment.  The  management   
reinforces that it will create a campus free from discrimination, harassment, retaliation or  
sexual assault at all levels. VU will ensure compliance with all provisions of the  regulation  
and make the following efforts toward the same:    
a)  Constitute  an   Internal  Complaints  Committee   to  proactively  curb  all  forms  of   
harassment of employees and students.    
b)  Publicly  notify  the  provisions  against  sexual  harassment  and  ensure  their  wide   
dissemination in the prospectus, notice boards as well as the website, the penalty and  
consequences of sexual harassment.    
c)  Organise training programmes/ workshops for the officers, functionaries , faculty and  
students, as indicated in the SAKSHAM Report (Measures for Ensuring the Safety of  
Women  and  Programmes  for  Gender  Sensitization  on  Campuses)  of  the  UGC,  to   
sensitize  them  and  ensure  knowledge  and  awareness  of  the  rights,  entitlements  and   
respon sibilities  enshrined  in  the  Act  and  under  these  regulations.  These  include   
sessions  to  create  awareness  about  what  constitutes  sexual  harassment  including   
hostile environment harassment and quid pro quo harassment   
d)  Act  decisively  against  all  gender -based  violence  perpetrated  against  employees  and   
students of all sexes.    
e)  Bring to book those guilty of sexual harassment against its employees and students.    
f)  Monitor the timely submission of reports by the ICC as well as prepare an annual status  
report with details on the number of cases filed and their disposal and submit the same  
to the Commission.

3.  Constitution of ICC   
VU has established an Internal Complaints Committee to prevent, prohibit and redress and  
issues of sexual harassment.  The ICC constitutes a lady presiding officer who is a senior  
teaching  faculty  member,  2  other  teaching  faculty  members,  2  members  from  th e  non - 
58

teaching,  3  students  and  an  external  member  who  works  for  an  association  that  is   
committed to the cause of women.    
4.  Role of ICC   
a)  provide  assistance  if  an  employee  or  a  student  chooses  to  file  a  complaint  with  the   
police;   
b)  provide mechanisms or dispute redressal and dialogue to  address  issues through a  
just and fair conciliation without undermining the complainant's rights, and minimize  
the need for purely punitive approaches that lead to further resentment, alienation or  
violence ;   
c)  protect the safety of the complainant by not divulging the person's identity, and provide  
the mandatory relief by way of sanctioned leave or relaxation or attendance requirement  
or transfer to another department or supervisor as required during the pendenc y of the  
complaint, or also provide for the transfer of the offender;   
d)  ensure  that  victims  or  witnesses  are  not  victimized  or  discriminated  against  while   
dealing with complaints of sexual harassment; and   
e)  ensure  the  prohibition  of  retaliation  or  adverse  action  against  a  covered  individual   
because the employee or the student is engaged in protected activity.   
5.  How to lodge a complaint?   
An  aggrieved  person  is  required  to  submit  a  written  complaint  to  the  ICC  within  three   
months from the date of the incident and in case of a series of incidents within a period of  
three months from the date of the last incident.    
The Presiding Officer or any Member of the ICC shall render all reasonable assistance to  
the person for making the complaint in writing.    
6.  Process and timeline of conducting an inquiry   
a)  The  ICC  shall,   upon  receipt  of   the  complaint,  send  one  copy  of  the  complaint  to  the   
respondent within a period of seven days of such receipt.   
b)  Upon receipt of the copy of the complaint, the respondent shall file his or her reply to  
the complaint along with the list of documents, and names and addresses of witnesses  
within a period of ten days.   
c)  The inquiry has to be completed within a period of ninety days from the receipt of the  
complaint.  The  inquiry  report,  with  recommendations,  if  any,  has  to  be  submitted   
within ten days from the completion of the inquiry to the Vice Chancellor of VU. Copy  
of  the  findings  or  recommendations  shall  also  be  served  on  both  parties  to  the   
complaint.   
59

d)  The Vice Chancellor shall act on the recommendations of the committee within a period  
of thirty days from the receipt of the inquiry report unless an appeal against the findings  
is filed within that time by either party.   
e)  An appeal against the findings or /recommendations of the ICC may be filed by either  
party  before  the  Vice  Chancellor  within  a  period  of  thirty  days  from  the  date  of  the   
recommendations.   
f)  The aggrieved party may seek conciliation in order to settle the matter.  No monetary  
settlement should be made as a basis of conciliation. The conciliation process shall be  
facilitated through the ICC   
g)  The identities of the aggrieved party or victim or the witness or the offender shall not be  
made public or kept in the public domain, especially during the process of the inquiry.   
7.  Action against offenders   
a)  Anyone found guilty of sexual harassment shall be punished in accordance with the  
service rules of VU  if the offender is an employee.   
b)  Where the respondent is a student, depending upon the severity of the offence VU may    
i)  withhold privileges of the student such as access to the library, auditoria, halls of  
residence, transportation, scholarships, allowances, and identity card;   
ii)  suspend or restrict entry into the campus for a specific period;   
iii)  expel and strike off the name from the rolls of VU, including denial of readmission,  
if the offence so warrants;   
iv)  award   reformative   punishments   like   mandatory   counselling   and,   or,   the    
performance of community services.

8.  Action Against False or frivolous Complaints   
To  ensure  that  the  provisions  for  the  protection  of  employees  and  students  from  sexual   
harassment do not get misused, provisions against false or malicious complaints have to be  
made.  If the ICC concludes that the allegations made were false, malicious or  the complaint  
was  made  knowing  it  to  be  untrue,  or  forged  or  misleading  information  has  been  provided   
during the inquiry, the complainant shall be liable to be punished.

Sports  policy  is  crucial  for  fostering  physical  health,  social  cohesion,  and  economic  growth   
within  a  society.  By  promoting  regular  physical  activity,  it  helps  combat  lifestyle -related  
diseases  and  enhances  mental  well -being.  It  encourages  inclusivity  and   social  integration,   
ensuring  equal  access  to  sports  for  all,  while  instilling  values  like  teamwork  and  discipline   
among  youth.  Economically,  sports  policy  generates  jobs,  boosts  local  economies  through   
sports tourism, and stimulates infrastructure investme nt.    
It  also  enhances  national  pride  by  supporting  elite  athletes  and  fostering  success  on  the   
international stage. Ensuring fairness and safety in sports, it promotes lifelong participation,  
contributing to overall life quality and community well -being.

1. Objectives:   
භ  Enhance  Physical  Health:  One  of  the  main  goals  is  to  encourage  everyone  in  the   
university  community  to  engage  in  regular  physical  activity.  By  doing  so,  we  aim  to   
improve  the  overall  health  and  well -being  of  all  students,  faculty,  and  staff.  Regular   
exerci se  can  lead  to  better  physical  fitness,  increased  energy  levels,  and  improved   
mental health.  
භ  Boost  Participation:  Another  important  objective  is  to  increase  the  number  of  people   
participating in sports and recreational activities. We want to create more opportunities  
for  everyone  to  get  involved,  whether  they  are  beginners  or  experienced  athletes.   By  
boosting  participation,  we  hope  to  create  a  more  active  and  engaged  university   
community.   
භ  Skill Development: We aim to provide various opportunities for students to develop and  
refine  their  sports  skills.  This  includes  offering  training  programs,  workshops,  and

per sonal growth and enhance their enjoyment of sports and physical activities.   
භ  Promote Team Spirit: Fostering a sense of teamwork, fair play, and sportsmanship is a  
key focus. We want to create an environment where everyone values cooperation and  
respect.  Through  team  sports  and  group  activities,  participants  can  learn  the   
importance  of working together, supporting each other, and competing with integrity.

to providing the necessary resources and support to help them achieve their best. This  
includes  access  to  high -quality  training  facilities,  professional  coaching,  and  ot her  
resources that can aid in their athletic development. By supporting elite athletes, we  
help them reach their full potential and represent the university with pride.

STUDENT EXAM ENROLLMENT PROCEDURE & HALL TICKET DOWNLOAD:
1) Login with credentials at Digii portal.

3) Click "Edit Enrollment".
4) Add all desired courses using the plus (+) button next to each course, then click "Save".
5) Payment: Check confirmation box, click "Pay & Enroll", then click "Pay Dues" to pay online.
6) Verification: Return to examination page to check status.
